title: Rolls-Royce Appoints Two New Members to North American Board

scenes.title: Announcement
scenes.text: Rolls-Royce announced the appointment of General Laura Richardson (U.S. Army, retired) and General Duke Richardson (U.S. Air Force, retired) to the Board of Directors for Rolls-Royce North America.

scenes.title: Laura Richardson Career
scenes.text: General Laura Richardson served more than 38 years in the U.S. Army and most recently commanded United States Southern Command, overseeing U.S. military operations and security cooperation across 31 countries in Central and South America and the Caribbean.

scenes.title: Laura Richardson Aviation Background
scenes.text: She began her career as an Army aviator flying Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk helicopters and commanded an assault helicopter battalion in Iraq.

scenes.title: Laura Richardson Leadership Roles
scenes.text: During her career, she also served in the White House, at the U.S. Capitol, and at the Pentagon, and previously led United States Army North.

scenes.title: Duke Richardson Career
scenes.text: General Duke Richardson retired after 42 years in the U.S. Air Force as Commander of Air Force Materiel Command.

scenes.title: Duke Richardson Responsibilities
scenes.text: He oversaw the full lifecycle of nearly all U.S. Air Force weapon systems, from research and testing to long-term maintenance and installation support.

scenes.title: Duke Richardson Previous Roles
scenes.text: He served as military deputy to the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Acquisition, Technology and Logistics and held four Program Executive Officer leadership positions across the Air Force and U.S. Special Operations Command.

scenes.title: Company Statement
scenes.text: Adam Riddle, President – Defense and CEO of Rolls-Royce North America, said the company is honored to welcome both leaders and highlighted their decades of leadership, strategic vision, and commitment to national defense.

scenes.title: Government Security Committee
scenes.text: Both new board members will also serve on the Government Security Committee as part of the Special Security Agreement with the U.S. Department of War.

scenes.title: Rolls-Royce North America
scenes.text: North America is the largest market for Rolls-Royce and plays a major role in the company's civil aerospace, defense, and power systems businesses.

scenes.title: U.S. Operations
scenes.text: All U.S. defense aerospace products are designed, engineered, manufactured, and assembled in Indianapolis, Indiana, the company's largest facility in the region.

scenes.title: Major Facilities
scenes.text: Other major sites include Aiken, South Carolina; Mankato, Minnesota; and Savannah, Georgia.

scenes.title: Investment in the U.S.
scenes.text: Over the past decade, Rolls-Royce North America has invested more than $1.5 billion in technology upgrades, facilities, and testing capabilities.

scenes.title: Economic Impact
scenes.text: The company employs over 5,000 people in the United States, supports hundreds of suppliers across 26 states, and contributed $6.2 billion to the U.S. economy in 2024.
